title: My first vibecoded game outside of Three.js: OG Clash (Kaigen Game Engine)
author: yerbamate2020
selftext:
I'm not a game dev, but like many here I've been vibe coding Three.js games with AI for the past few months and having a lot of fun with it.

Last week I came across a demo of Kaigen, a newer game engine, on X and wanted to give it a try. I DM'd the creator and he gave me access to experiment with it.

After spending a week building a game with it, a few thoughts:

* I still love Three.js. It's incredibly fast to build with, has a huge ecosystem, and models know it really well. Hard to beat for getting something playable up quickly.
* That said, I've been looking for something with more of the benefits of a full game engine (renderer, physics, animations, better performance at scale) without the overhead of Unity or Unreal.
* Kaigen was pretty impressive on that front. The renderer and performance were noticeably better for what I was trying to build, and I was able to get results I hadn't managed to achieve with Three.js in the same amount of time.
* The biggest downside was token usage. It took a lot more tokens and back-and-forth to build compared to a similar Three.js game, which makes sense given how much more familiar models are with Three.js.

I also made a cinematic trailer for the game entirely in Claude Code, which was a fun experiment in itself.

Has anyone else tried building games with newer engines instead of Three.js or Unity? Interested in what people have found works best with coding agents.
